idiom_name: constant path + Module#const_get, with Zeitwerk autoloading as the convention
implementation_notes: Ruby's registry is the constant table: a class or module reference is resolved by name, Object.const_get("Acme::SqlRepository") loads the constant on demand and raises NameError when the name is wrong, and Zeitwerk maps a constant path to a file path so the lookup needs no explicit require. That means the classic locator class is usually replaced by naming conventions plus a plain Hash of factories built at the composition root, and it is also why Ruby applications rarely carry a DI container. Reserve const_get for names that genuinely come from configuration and prefer a Hash keyed by symbols for the common case; where a whole object graph is involved, constructor arguments and mixin modules stay the language-appropriate answer.
code_sketch:
REGISTRY = {}                                   # token -> factory

def register(token, &factory)
  REGISTRY[token] ||= factory
end

def resolve(token)
  factory = REGISTRY[token] or raise KeyError, "unregistered service: #{token}"
  factory.call
end

# configuration-driven alternative:
# Object.const_get("Acme::#{name.capitalize}Repository").new
pitfalls: Ruby reloads constants, not classes: an object captured in an initializer keeps the stale class after a Rails reload, which is why Zeitwerk/Rails forbid referencing reloadable constants during initialization.

const_get walks ancestors unless inherit=false, so a name that collides with an inherited constant resolves to the wrong object instead of failing; Zeitwerk raises Zeitwerk::NameError when a file defines a different constant than its path promises.

Writing to a global Hash from several threads or from required files is unsynchronized, and reopening classes to install implementations is a global operation - do both during boot, not at request time.
